title: Build fails on macOS with implicit Lua function declarations
body: I'm building Neovim from source on macOS 13 at commit 93d99aefd314bc4abfc54c0c29a4de84b6fcc823. The build fails while compiling files such as src/nvim/lua/spell.c because functions including luaL_register are reported as implicit declarations, and all the errors are of that kind. I cloned the repository, ran a Release build, and expected compilation to succeed. The compiler command uses AppleClang from Xcode and includes both /opt/local/include and the bundled LuaJIT include directory.

symptoms_visible: My Neovim source build on macOS 13 stops while compiling C files such as lua/spell.c because luaL_register and other functions are reported as implicit declarations.
N0.label: N0 macOS source build failure reported

symptoms_visible: The older revision I checked builds normally, while the build produces the implicit-declaration errors after I check out the later revision.
N1.label: N1 regression revision confirmed

symptoms_visible: After wiping the repository, cloning it again, and refreshing the shell command cache, the build still stops with the same implicit-declaration errors.
N2_x.label: N2_x clean-build aftermath

symptoms_visible: The clean verbose build still fails; its compile command contains /opt/local/include before the bundled luajit-2.1 include directory.
N3.label: N3 verbose include paths collected

symptoms_visible: On the MacPorts setup, the source build succeeds after Lua 5.3 is removed and fails again after Lua 5.3 is reinstalled; reinstalling LuaJIT alone still allows it to build.
N4.label: N4 MacPorts Lua package interaction reproduced

symptoms_visible: With the updated candidate change, the build completes and the resulting Neovim executable reports LuaJIT 2.1.0-beta3.
N5.label: N5 candidate fix verified

symptoms_visible: Neovim now compiles successfully on my MacPorts-based macOS setup, and the resulting executable uses LuaJIT.
N_terminal.label: terminal build succeeds

question_patterns: Can you bisect or manually test revisions to identify when the build started failing?
Could you confirm whether the suspected revision is the point where the failure appears?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I checked out 9b1112c and it builds normally. After checking out https://github.com/neovim/neovim/commit/438b4361cc761a2950689668f008cfe06c1510f7, I can confirm that the build fails.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both revisions fail with the same errors, including the older revision.
The same good and bad revisions are confirmed from a proper automated bisection rather than manual checkouts.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c1 and c3: rebelot manually tested an older working revision and the suspected later revision. The answer preserves the raw checkout results rather than adding the later header-selection diagnosis.

solution.intent: Remove stale build artifacts and retry from a fully clean checkout using the appropriate Apple developer tools.
solution.concrete_example: Run make distclean before switching revisions, or recreate the checkout completely, and make sure the active Command Line Developer Tools match the installed macOS version.

edges.comment: Maintainer suggestions c6-c7 and reporter response c8: rebelot had wiped and recloned the repository and still observed the error. Cleaning is therefore a real falsified attempt, not the resolution.

question_patterns: Can you run a fresh verbose CMake build and paste the complete compile command for a failing source file?
Please build with cmake --build build --verbose after cleaning and share the full output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran a clean verbose CMake build and shared the logs. The failing compile command has -isystem /Users/laurenzi/usr/src/neovim/.deps/usr/include, then -isystem /opt/local/include, and then -isystem /Users/laurenzi/usr/src/neovim/.deps/usr/include/luajit-2.1.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failing compile command contains only the bundled LuaJIT include directories and no /opt/local/include path.
The same include paths appear in the verbose log, but the build directory is generated with Unix Makefiles instead of Ninja.

question_patterns: What LuaJIT, pkg-config, and dependency paths does CMake report during configuration?
Please include the CMake dependency-detection output from the clean build.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: CMake says it found LuaJIT at /Users/laurenzi/usr/src/neovim/.deps/usr/lib/libluajit-5.1.a and uses the bundled luajit interpreter, but it also finds PkgConfig at /opt/local/bin/pkg-config and Gettext under /opt/local.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c12, c15, c19, and c20: rebelot supplied complete and verbose logs. In c15 and c17 the reporter also disclosed that Lua and CMake came from MacPorts; that unprompted setup fact is recorded in N3.volunteered_info.

question_patterns: Can you temporarily remove the separately installed Lua packages and repeat the build, then restore them one at a time?
Does the result change when the external Lua installation is absent?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After uninstalling lua53, luarocks, and luajit while keeping lua52, building from master succeeds. Reinstalling luajit still succeeds. After reinstalling lua53, the build fails again; luarocks also pulls Lua 5.3 as a dependency.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The build still fails after every MacPorts Lua package is removed, and reinstalling Lua 5.3 makes no difference.
Lua 5.4 rather than Lua 5.3 is the external package whose installation makes the same build fail.

edges.comment: Affected-user messages c24-c27 and c33 are folded into the simulated user side. The second MacPorts user performed the controlled package-removal test on a separate aarch64 Mac; no architecture-specific setup is spliced into rebelot's system, but the shared MacPorts package interaction is retained as corroborating evidence.

question_patterns: Could you test the updated candidate change again and report whether a clean build completes?
Please try the latest revision of the linked pull request and tell me what the build does.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It works perfectly. The build completes, and nvim -v reports LuaJIT 2.1.0-beta3.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The updated candidate still fails with luaL_register reported as an implicit declaration.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c36 and c38 confirm the final revision of the candidate change. The earlier successful test in c22 and the final retests all report observable build results; interpretation of why the change works remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Correct Neovim's CMake include handling so the intended bundled LuaJIT headers take precedence over incompatible Lua 5.3 or 5.4 headers exposed globally by MacPorts, while retaining system-header treatment where appropriate.
solution.concrete_example: Adjust the CMake include setup so the bundled luajit-2.1 include directory is searched before the blanket /opt/local/include path. This prevents MacPorts' Lua 5.3 lua.h from being selected while Neovim is being compiled against bundled LuaJIT.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied include-path ordering, dependency-detection output, and build results. Maintainers combined that evidence with the MacPorts package experiment to conclude that an incompatible Lua 5.3 or 5.4 lua.h from /opt/local/include was shadowing the bundled LuaJIT header. That header-selection diagnosis is engineer inference, not something the reporter knew from the initial compiler error.

edges.comment: Final diagnosis from c28-c34 and validation from c35-c38: MacPorts exposes a blanket /opt/local/include containing an incompatible Lua header, and the accepted CMake change ensures Neovim uses the intended LuaJIT headers. Both rebelot and the second affected MacPorts user validated the candidate; the reporter's final test establishes resolution on the opening setup.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: MacPorts exposes an incompatible Lua 5.3 or 5.4 lua.h through /opt/local/include, which is selected ahead of the bundled LuaJIT header and causes LuaJIT API functions such as luaL_register to appear undeclared.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the verbose include ordering and the controlled MacPorts package test where removing Lua 5.3 makes the build succeed and reinstalling it makes the failure return.
The fix must correct CMake include handling so the intended bundled LuaJIT headers take precedence; uninstalling MacPorts Lua may be mentioned only as a diagnostic or temporary workaround.

Must not present make distclean, recloning, changing CPU architecture, or switching compilers as the resolution; a completely fresh clone still failed and another affected user reproduced the issue on aarch64.
Must have the reporter verify a build containing the updated include-handling change before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced source-build user who can switch Git revisions, run CMake and Ninja directly, capture verbose compiler logs, inspect compiler and include paths, and test a pull request; not initially familiar with the interaction between MacPorts' global include directory and Lua headers.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise, cooperative, and technically detailed when asked; pastes commands and complete logs, reports direct test outcomes, and asks practical questions about dependency-search configuration.
